overall: The AG found the Curriculum and Instruction Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to create and maintain minutes for all its meetings, rejecting the timeliness defense; it declined to review the insufficient-minutes, minutes-request, notice-vote, and documents allegations.

allegations.summary: Subcommittee failed to create and maintain meeting minutes for its meetings since its 2012 inception.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the information provided by the Committee, we find that the Subcommittee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to create and maintain minutes for all of its meetings.

allegations.summary: Subcommittee's meeting minutes were allegedly insufficient in content.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint does not identify any specific minutes that are alleged to be insufficient; any particular request for minutes that the Subcommittee failed to respond to; or any particular meeting for which the notice is alleged to have been insufficient.

allegations.summary: Subcommittee allegedly did not provide meeting minutes upon request.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint does not identify any specific minutes that are alleged to be insufficient; any particular request for minutes that the Subcommittee failed to respond to; or any particular meeting for which the notice is alleged to have been insufficient.

allegations.summary: Subcommittee allegedly took votes without stating on meeting notices that it would do so.
allegations.key_passage: in general it is reasonably foreseeable that a public body may take action and hold a vote following discussion of a topic listed on a meeting notice; the Open Meeting Law does not require that the notice separately indicate the possibility of a vote.

allegations.summary: Subcommittee allegedly failed to make documents used at its meetings publicly available.
allegations.key_passage: requests for such documents are governed by the Public Records Law, not the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.

Create minutes for all past meetings for which it has not yet done so, to the best of its ability and through whatever means are available, including the memories and individual notations of the attendees.

Within 90 days of receipt of the letter, certify to the AG's office that it has complied with the order to create meeting minutes, or explain in writing what efforts it made for meetings where minutes cannot be created.
remedy_passage: We order the Subcommittee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
